messages:
leo (newhire): Hey folks, first-day setup question. Running our docker-compose locally on my M1 Mac and both postgres and redis keep exiting. Logs show postgres complaining about socket in use and redis says could not bind to 127.0.0.1:6379

leo (newhire): postgres log: ERROR: could not create socket \"/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432\": Address already in use

leo (newhire): redis log: bind: Address already in use

maya: Welcome! Sounds like system services on your Mac are already listening on those ports. macOS sometimes starts Postgres (via brew services) or another DB. Try: `brew services list` and `brew services stop postgresql` (or the specific service).

sam (devex): Another option that avoids stopping system services: change the host-side ports in compose. Example: `15432:5432` and `16379:6379` then point your app to localhost:15432 and localhost:16379.

sam (devex): Also note: some Postgres clients prefer unix sockets when host is empty, so explicitly set PGHOST=127.0.0.1 or DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:pass@127.0.0.1:15432/dbname to force TCP instead of socket lookup.

leo (newhire): ah ok — I was using psql without -h so it tried the socket. nice catch.

tj: For Redis, the default image binds to 127.0.0.1 in some configs; if you want it reachable from other containers keep container network defaults (no extra host binding), but if you map ports adjust the bind or use `bind 0.0.0.0` in redis.conf. In compose you can override with `command: ["redis-server", "--bind", "0.0.0.0"]`

maya: FYI on M1 you may hit architecture issues with certain images. We pin images in the repo (`postgres:14-alpine`, `redis:6-alpine`) which are multi-arch. If you see "exec format error" add `platform: linux/amd64` temporarily.

leo (newhire): I tweaked ports and set PGHOST=127.0.0.1, now postgres starts but redis still exits with `Permission denied` when writing appendonly.aof to mounted volume (mounted host dir).

sam (devex): Permission denied on mac host mounts is common. Quick fixes:

sam (devex): - `docker-compose down -v` then `docker-compose up` (clean the volume).

sam (devex): - If using a bind mount to a host path, ensure the directory exists and has permissive perms. Example: `mkdir -p ./tmp/redisdata && chmod 0777 ./tmp/redisdata` then mapping that path.

maya: If you'd rather avoid fiddling with mounts, use a named volume in compose (Docker manages permissions better):

maya: ```yaml
services:
  redis:
    image: redis:6-alpine
    ports:
      - "16379:6379"
    volumes:
      - redis-data:/data

volumes:
  redis-data:
```

leo (newhire): great, created a named volume and redis stayed up. thanks!

tj: Pro tip: to connect from host to container on Mac use `127.0.0.1` or `localhost` and mapped port. To connect container-to-container use the service name (e.g., `postgres:5432`).

devx-bot: https://redwood-inference.internal/docs/onboarding/local-services.md :point_right: "Local Postgres & Redis tips"

leo (newhire): this was super helpful. one more: how do I make sure my local changes to compose don't break CI?

sam (devex): Keep local overrides in `docker-compose.override.yml` or `docker-compose.local.yml` and don't commit them. Our repo has `docker-compose.ci.yml` for CI expectations. We also run `make local-up` which sets the sane defaults for dev.

leo (newhire): perfect — thanks y'all :heart:
